brief_summary: Left-to-right process strip showing the group-buy status lifecycle — announced, live, closed, shipped — with a branch point after 'closed' peeling off to a 'delayed' checkpoint (highlighted amber, dashed) and a 'cancelled' checkpoint (outlined in the caution-red token). Illustrates that a listing's status badge is a lifecycle to be read, not a single static label.
data_sources: how-to-evaluate-a-group-buy.mdx § 'Check the runner before the render' — 'a listing's status badge moves through a known lifecycle, and a vendor's archive of past buys on the vendor directory shows whether prior runs actually closed out and shipped, or whether they're still sitting in a stalled state months past their estimate.'

packages/data/src/schemas/group-buy.ts — status enum: 'announced', 'live', 'closed', 'shipped', 'delayed', 'cancelled', with statusNote (text, sourceUrl, asOf) required when status is 'delayed' or 'cancelled'.

how-to-evaluate-a-group-buy.mdx § 'Reading the timeline for red flags' — 'A delayed status that comes with a dated, sourced explanation is a far better sign than a listing that simply never updates and leaves the buyer to guess.'
